notes:
Summary: CavernBay AssistNet provides an omnichannel support platform for mid-size telco operators. They're piloting agent-assist and automated summarization to reduce AHT and improve first-contact resolution. Primary ask: robust RAG over multiple KBs (Zendesk, Confluence, internal SFTP dumps) with citation provenance, freshness control, and deterministic fallback rules during spikes.

Recent timeline & cues:
- 2026-02-03: Intro call (Jordan Ortiz, VP Support). Wants clear citations for agents: "I need to see the paragraph and link that backs an answer."
- 2026-02-14: Technical discovery w/ SE Priya Nair. Confirmed sources: Zendesk + Confluence + nightly SFTP export + historical ticket archive (10 years).
- 2026-02-20: POC kickoff (Fireflies ff_20260220_0182). Agreed scope: ingestion pipeline, incremental indexing, retrieval + re-ranker, agent UI snippet, tool-calling demo (ticket update, escalate).
- 2026-03-01: POC milestone 1 passed: vector index built for top 10k articles; baseline retrieval latency 120ms p50 on dedicated test instance.
- 2026-03-05: Security questionnaire returned; main concerns = live KB read access, KMS integration, retention controls, audit trail for each generated answer.

POC details / success metrics (customer-defined):
- Precision w/ citations: >= 85% of returned answers include exact doc paragraph and link.
- Freshness SLA: changes in source propagated within 15 minutes for Confluence critical pages (ops runbook).
- Latency: agent assist response <300ms p95 during normal load; degrade gracefully under spikes (defined below).
- Reliability: support during seasonal spike simulation (50k concurrent sessions) with fallback to cached summaries and read-only mode if capacity constrained.
- Cost targets: keep incremental infra cost < $25k/month for production footprint.

Technical requirements called out by their infra team:
- Must support live connectors to Zendesk and Confluence with incremental syncs and webhooks for near-real-time updates.
- Two-tier index: hot (last 30 days) in memory for sub-100ms retrieval; warm/cold on disk for older docs.
- Explicit provenance per answer (doc id, paragraph offset, timestamp, hash). UI should display source age and confidence.
- Tool-calling: ability for model to send structured actions to internal ticketing API (create/update/escalate) with RBAC and audit logging.
- Encryption: BYOK/KMS for all at-rest keys; HSM optional for private customers.
- Data residency: EU data to remain in eu-central-1 for their EU customers.

Customer quotes / color:
- "We need deterministic behaviors when the model hallucinates — show me the source or don't show the answer." — VP Support
- "If we can't prove freshness, agents won't trust the suggestions." — Head of Operations

Current POC status & notes:
- Infrastructure: team spun up a dedicated test cluster in our staging GCP project. Early perf looks good but p95 increases to ~900ms when concurrent retriever jobs spike in the sim. Need batching and prefix caching suggestions from Redwood Optimize.
- Retrieval quality: initial embeddings (open-source model) ok; mismatch on short Qs vs long runbooks. SE suggested trying a hybrid retriever (dense + sparse) and Reranker model.
- Tool-calling policy: security requires an allowlist and human confirmation flow for any ticket-closing action. Working through UX constraints.

Next steps (short):
- SE Priya to deliver architecture diagram + cost estimate for dedicated deployment by 2026-03-12.
- Security call scheduled 2026-03-16 to walk through KMS, audit logs, and data residency flows.
- Customer wants a small-scale spike test (20k concurrent) before committing to full seasonal simulation. Scope: stress test retrieval + fallback policy.

Open questions / risks:
- Cost for vector DB if hosted (egress + IOPS) vs self-hosted on Dedicated GPUs.
- Can Redwood provide sub-15 minute freshness for large Confluence spaces with heavy edit churn?
- SLA penalties if agent assist goes into degraded mode during peak season — they want clear runbook and auto-fallback.
